content.text:
I fixed `addMonths` in `dates.js`. Dates on the 31st now land on the last day of a shorter month, as the comment above the function already described.

**Cause:** `setMonth` alone overflows. Jan 31 + 1 month became "Feb 31", which rolls into Mar 3. Those customers were being billed in the wrong month.

**Fix:** The function now clamps the day. It sets the day to 1, changes the month, then sets the day to the smaller of the original day and the length of the target month. The time of day is kept, and the input date isn't changed.

I ran it by hand with a 10:30 time of day:

| Input | Months added | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Jan 31 2026 | 1 | Feb 28 2026 |
| Mar 31 2026 | 1 | Apr 30 2026 |
| Jan 31 2026 | 2 | Mar 31 2026 |
| Jan 31 2024 | 1 | Feb 29 2024 (leap year) |
| Dec 31 2026 | 2 | Feb 28 2027 |
| Jan 15 2026 | -2 | Nov 15 2025 |

I didn't run `npm test`.

One thing to know about the billing logic: if you chain calls, Jan 31 → Feb 28 → Mar 28, the day drifts. To keep billing on the 31st, compute each date from the original start date with `addMonths(start, n)`.

**Cause:** `setMonth` alone overflows. Jan 31 + 1 month became "Feb 31", which rolls into Mar 3. Those customers were being billed in the wrong month.

**Fix:** The function now clamps the day. It sets the day to 1, changes the month, then sets the day to the smaller of the original day and the length of the target month. The time of day is kept, and the input date isn't changed.

I ran it by hand with a 10:30 time of day:

|---|---|---|

One thing to know about the billing logic: if you chain calls, Jan 31 → Feb 28 → Mar 28, the day drifts. To keep billing on the 31st, compute each date from the original start date with `addMonths(start, n)`.
